title: Existing VLANs fail after VLAN 30 is added
scenario: SW1 Gi0/1 connects to SW2 Gi0/1. Each switch has one correctly addressed PC in VLAN 10 (192.168.10.0/24), VLAN 20 (192.168.20.0/24) and VLAN 30 (192.168.30.0/24). Same-VLAN communication across the link worked for VLANs 10 and 20 before a change intended to add VLAN 30. Now only the new VLAN 30 pair communicates across it. Both switch consoles are available. The following excerpts are representative teaching evidence.

exhibits.title: SW1 trunk summary
exhibits.text:
Port        Mode   Encapsulation   Status      Native vlan
Gi0/1       on     802.1q          trunking    99

Vlans allowed on trunk: 30
Vlans allowed and active: 30
Vlans forwarding and not pruned: 30

exhibits.title: Recorded configuration of SW1 Gi0/1
exhibits.text:
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk native vlan 99
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 30
 switchport nonegotiate

exhibits.title: Checks completed on both switches
exhibits.text:
VLANs 10,20,30,99 exist and are active locally.
PC access-port assignments and /24 addresses match the design.
SW2 Gi0/1 is trunking, native 99, with 10,20,30,99 allowed and forwarding.

question: Which diagnosis fits all the evidence?
options: Creating VLAN 30 replaced VLAN 20 in the VLAN database.
The allowed list on SW1 was replaced by 30 instead of extended.
The link changed into an access connection in VLAN 30.
The native VLAN on SW1 changed from 99 to 30.
explanation: SW1 remains an operational trunk with native VLAN 99. Its allowed list contains only 30, even though the original VLANs still exist. That selective filter explains why the new pair works and the old same-VLAN pairs fail.
fix:
Use SW1's console to restore the required VLANs while retaining 30.

```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/1
SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 10,20,99
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show interfaces trunk
```

The allowed list should become 10,20,30,99. Verify local activity and forwarding, then repeat each same-VLAN pair's test in both directions. Do not assume the list alone proves host connectivity. Save after verification and correct the change instructions to distinguish replacement from add.

title: Native VLAN agreement is missing on a replacement switch
scenario: The intended native VLAN between SW1 Gi0/1 and SW2 Gi0/1 is 99. A test PC on each switch uses an access port in VLAN 99, with addresses 10.99.0.11/24 and 10.99.0.12/24 and no gateway. Their same-subnet test stopped working after SW2 was replaced. Separate tagged VLAN 10 tests still work in this reported incident. The displays below are representative configuration evidence, not a guarantee of identical protection behavior on every platform.

exhibits.title: SW1 Gi0/1 configuration
exhibits.text:
switchport mode trunk
switchport trunk native vlan 99
switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,99
switchport nonegotiate

exhibits.title: Replacement SW2 Gi0/1 configuration
exhibits.text:
switchport mode trunk
switchport trunk native vlan 1
switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,99
switchport nonegotiate

exhibits.title: Completed local checks
exhibits.text:
Both physical uplink ports are connected and configured as trunks.
VLAN 99 exists and is active on each switch.
The two test PC ports are static access VLAN 99 and linked.
PC addresses and masks match the stated 10.99.0.0/24 design.

question: What configuration defect must be repaired?
options: The test PCs need default gateways for their same-subnet traffic.
The switches must negotiate DTP before native frames can pass.
The replacement switch's native VLAN is 1 instead of the agreed 99.
VLAN 99 must be removed from both allowed lists.
explanation: The native settings differ explicitly. Under default treatment, an ordinary untagged frame sent from SW1 as VLAN 99 is not classified as VLAN 99 by SW2. Native mismatches may also trigger spanning-tree protection; neither a working tagged VLAN nor the absence of a particular warning makes this configuration correct.
fix:
Restore the documented native VLAN on the replacement switch through its console.

```ios SW2
SW2# configure terminal
SW2(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/1
SW2(config-if)# switchport trunk native vlan 99
SW2(config-if)# end
SW2# show interfaces trunk
```

Compare both native and allowed settings, allow any protective state to recover, and repeat the VLAN 99 and VLAN 10 tests. If a state remains nonforwarding, inspect its evidence rather than disabling spanning tree. Update the replacement template and save the verified configuration.
